title: Proposed collaboration on MAP2K1-related CFC syndrome

sentences.text: Exploring a research collaboration on MAP2K1-related cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome
We are writing to CFC International, and would also value the views of the RASopathies Network.
MAP2K1 changes are linked to gain of function, but this is contested: the variants still depend on activation by RAF.
The CITIZEN CFC Syndrome Registry, PATRAS and the RASopathies Network contact registry include people with this condition.
A clinical, genetic and epidemiologic study of RASopathies is recruiting.
A RASopathy biorepository and a cardiomyopathy natural history study are recruiting, and the Baby MERIT trial is not yet recruiting, though these enrol by syndrome and do not name MAP2K1.
We would like to explore a jointly designed study on MAP2K1-related CFC syndrome, shaped with your community from the start: [study question], [design], [sites].
Any participation would follow informed consent and ethics approval, and we would share what we learn with your community.

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to a conversation about whether this idea is useful to the families you serve?
If so, we would value your view on how your community, registry or natural history work could take part, with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
Could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you, perhaps [proposed dates]?
With thanks and warm regards, [researcher name], [institution].
